editorial_corrections: 1500 Bristol Common Council merchants' company is a local commercial fellowship, NOT identical to Anglo-Portuguese syndicate of 1501/1502 patents; those patents granted named persons rights, not company incorporation.
1505 Michael of Bristol Cape-merchant suit concerns freight/trade, evidence relates to Andalucía and does NOT prove Newfoundland landfall by Michael.

1502 £100 reward in Jones (2010) pertains to a declared butlerage account relating to 1502; the original source does not establish the exact 1500-1502 range suggested by earlier researcher metadata. Treat specific payment date as unknown within/account 1502.

1500 Calais quarter/half-year treaty 25,000 francs is an obligation per instalment, not actual verified receipts or British colonial profit. In 1501 archive shows receipt after deductions without amount independently reconciled.
Do not count 1502 £20 ship purchase bounty, 1502 September £20 voyage reward, and £100 butlerage payment as net profits nor sum unless underlying ledgers prove they are discrete transfers.
An English merchant trading with Ireland in 1504 does not itself show any violent forced colonial extraction or actual English sovereignty over the Irish unloading town.
